bullets.title: CRWV: GS upgrades to Buy ($106 PT, 73% upside); financing stress narrative overdone
bullets.body: Goldman upgrades CoreWeave to Buy from Neutral with $106 PT (stock down 43% since Aug 11, 24% in 5 days), arguing unlevered IRR upside is underestimated and WACC overestimated. Meanwhile, HPC index yield hit all-time high of 9.75% (+75bp on week), CRWV bond yields cited at ~16% unsecured, and the stock fell 15% mid-week on Musk/Palihapitiya commentary. Wolfe/JPM counter that CRWV has ~$125-130B backlog, can finance existing commitments, and GPU ASPs rose 25% in Q3 with another 10% across the board — financing costs would need to exceed 20% to neutralize improved unit economics.

bullets.title: INTC: JPMorgan upgrades to Neutral on execution improvement; stock +4.4% pre-market
bullets.body: JPM upgrades Intel to Neutral (from Underweight) as stock approaches fair value after 29.5% pullback, citing improved execution under new leadership. DCAI/server is now INTC's largest profit pool ($2.5B Q2 operating income), Granite Rapids demand extremely tight with LTA visibility into CY27, and ASIC services tracking $2B run-rate with path to $4B. UBS models CQ3 revenue near $17B with GM above 42% guide, EMIB-T yields improving from ~30% to ~60% by early 2027; UBS maintains Neutral with PT cut to $103 from $112.

bullets.title: ANET/CLS: UBS reiterates Buy on both; 15-20% pullback seen as de-risked entry
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on Arista and Celestica, expecting strong hyperscaler and enterprise demand to drive September-quarter results similar to June strength in networking and optical. Both names pulled back 15-20% on AI financing concerns but UBS views them as largely de-risked. JPM similarly calls out ANET and CLS as best risk/reward ahead of results.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: JPM favors STX on HAMR lead; cuts both PTs to mid-teens multiples on capex uncertainty
bullets.body: JPM expects STX to beat F1Q27 with $4.2B revenue/$7.58 EPS (vs $7.10-7.50 guide), while WDC faces product transition headwinds. STX's HAMR ramp is ~50% of nearline EB shipments by CY26-end; WDC's EB growth faces near-term lull in 1H27 before reaccelerating 25%+. JPM cuts both target multiples from high-teens to mid-teens on AI capex durability scrutiny, taking STX PT to $1,050 and WDC to $600 — both Overweight maintained on robust LTA demand.

bullets.title: MRVL: MSFT Maia 300 multi-GW deployments could be a major custom-silicon driver
bullets.body: UBS highlights MSFT Maia 300 (TSMC N2P, 8 HBM4 stacks, 950W TDP) entering production in 2027 with multi-GW scale planned — implying ~550K Maia accelerators per GW and millions of units at ~$4K ASP for MRVL (ex-HBM). MRVL exposure to Maia could become increasingly meaningful beyond 2027; separately MRVL is reiterating custom silicon opportunity above $12B in FY29. Minor Vera Rubin ramp delay (~1.5-2 months) noted but no revenue-rec impact.

bullets.title: AMZN/META/MSFT: Morgan Stanley raises PTs into earnings; hyperscaler capex raised sharply
bullets.body: MS moves AMZN to Top Pick with $350 PT (~40% upside) on AWS path to $1T revenue, Bedrock/agentic wins, and $16.50 FY28 EPS; raises AWS capex by $30B in 2027E to $300B. META PT raised to $820 (23x 27/28 EPS) with Muse GPU-constrained but 100M DAUs could consume 1-4GW annually. MSFT PT $600 (25x FY28E ~$24 EPS) with 4.25GW capacity coming online FY27 and E3-E5/Copilot adoption. AI capex now drives ~25% of 2027 SPX sales growth per MS.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye removes long on Rubin delay; GS raises server TAM 31-45% but stock sentiment cautious
bullets.body: Hedgeye exits NVDA long citing supply chain sources pointing to Rubin mass production delay to Q2 2027 (vs buyside expectation of late Q4/early Q1) and neocloud financing stress risking GPU order cancellations. Contrarily, GS raises AI chip demand forecast to 18M/29M/38M units in 2026-28E and raises NVL72 AI server shipments to 110K/164K racks in 2027/28E. Hedgeye risk ranges: NVDA in Bearish trend; AMZN and GOOGL also downgraded to Bearish.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Mizuho raises PT to $460 on TPU upside; at 200-day MA support ahead of earnings
bullets.body: Mizuho maintains Outperform on GOOGL with $460 PT (+35%), projecting $100B TPU revenues in 2028 (11%/9% above consensus on revenue/OI), though cuts multiple to 23x P/E from 30x. Jefferies flags GOOGL at 200-day MA support as a key debate: can the multiple hold if Search decelerates? Hedgeye downgrades GOOGL trend to Bearish.

bullets.title: NFLX: CCO Bajaria fired, replaced by Peter Rice; Brazil price hike up to 20%
bullets.body: Netflix replaced Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria (10-year tenure) with Peter Rice from Disney/Fox. Co-CEO Sarandos admitted engagement 'not growing as fast as I want.' Netflix also raised Brazil Premium tier prices up to 20%. SPOT JPM note flags long SPOT/short NFLX as a popular pair trade with NFLX down 25% YTD vs SPOT down 9%.

bullets.title: SPOT: Needs clean Q3 + AI product launch to break $450-550 range
bullets.body: JPM flags SPOT stuck in $450-550 range since May; Q3 expectations include Premium Subs +1M above the +5M guide, GM beat of +20-30bps above 32.9% guide, and Q4 GM guide ~+50bps Q/Q. Investor expectations for the AI remixing product launch have slipped from Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, pending WMG and Sony licensing deals. Earnings Thursday with consensus €2.81 EPS on €4.98B revenue.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo demand strong but supply constrained; 94-day avg delivery, foldable sold out
bullets.body: JPM reports iPhone Duo preorder delivery dates average 94 days, signaling strong demand ahead of supply ramp and supporting the premiumization thesis. The foldable iPhone sold out online with delivery pushed to late January. Chinese media reports disappoint on price cuts pressuring retailers. AAPL at a 20-year high NTM P/E of 35.5x — Jefferies notes this is positioning-driven, not bullish fundamentals, as AAPL is now inversely correlated to NDX for the first time in history.

bullets.title: SHOP: Piper bullish on agentic merchant migrations; needs 30%+ revenue growth to satisfy investors
bullets.body: Piper Sandler positive on Shopify, citing agentic tools driving merchant migrations and expected merchant count acceleration. SHOP needs low-mid 30s% y/y revenue growth and a 4Q26 guide of low-30s% to satisfy investors; margins supported by structural employee cost reductions of $5M y/y. JPM hosting Shopify Platinum Partner call discussing AI-commerce strategy and SMB demand trends.

bullets.title: TXN: UBS top pick into year-end; data center growing 73-75% Y/Y, Q4 guide likely above Street
bullets.body: UBS selects TXN as top pick through year-end on durable analog cycle growth — CY26/27 analog revenue growing ~28%/19% Y/Y with data center up ~2x/~60%. UBS sees Q4 guidance likely at $5.8-5.9B vs Street, driven by pricing improvements and data center ramp. Industrial/auto revenue still 12%/9% below prior peaks, suggesting further upside duration. Reports Wednesday with consensus $2.43 EPS.

bullets.title: TSLA: Morgan Stanley turns more constructive ahead of Q3 earnings
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Andrew Jonas flagged a more constructive turn on Tesla ahead of Q3 earnings, which report Tuesday. OpCo expects improved margins on stronger EV sales and manufacturing efficiencies; Cybercab deployment progress and Optimus ramp timing are key debates. Hedgeye maintains TSLA in Bearish trend with buy level $348, sell $373.

bullets.title: HOOD: Hedgeye downgrades to Short Bench; KeyBanc favors for through-cycle growth
bullets.body: Hedgeye moves Robinhood from Best Idea Long to Short Bench in weekly position rebalancing. Contrarily, KeyBanc FinTech preview tactically favors HOOD as a through-cycle growth name. Robinhood is also set to become the first retail brokerage to offer SEC-approved binary options tied to company KPIs.

bullets.title: ABNB: Hedgeye upgrades to Best Idea Long on faster traffic growth and margin upside
bullets.body: Hedgeye moves ABNB from Long Bias to Best Idea Long. Jefferies notes ABNB as bullish on faster traffic growth and potential margin upside. September US RevPAR +11% YoY (first double-digit monthly growth since March 2023) provides positive backdrop.

bullets.title: ACN: Shares -2% on reports of $1.5B China operations sale
bullets.body: Financial Times reports Accenture is exploring a sale of its Greater China operations for up to $1.5B, allowing the company to refocus on global AI strategy. Shares fell ~2% in premarket. MS estimates Accenture targeting mid-single-digit organic growth FY27-28, accelerating to mid-to-high single digits FY29.

bullets.title: Semis sector: SOX down 8-9 consecutive sessions (longest since 2006/2008); de-rated to 17x from 29x
bullets.body: The SOX fell 8-9 consecutive sessions wiping out $2.3T in market cap — the longest losing streak since October 2008. Semis have de-rated from ~29x forward P/E in summer to ~17x, a ~25% relative drawdown vs SPX. The NDX forward P/E hit its lowest level of the decade (ex-Covid) at ~20.5x. Monday pre-market saw a 3.6% bounce in SOXX on technical dynamics and AI data center optimism from SemiAnalysis's 51GW 2027 buildout forecast.

bullets.title: TEAM: KeyBanc raises PT to $235; usage-based pricing and Rovo driving upside
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises Atlassian PT to $235 from $185 (26x FY28 EV/FCF), cautiously optimistic into F1Q27. Usage-based pricing expected to impact 60-80% of customers by year-end, potentially driving Collections upsell. Cloud revenue growth could accelerate from F4Q's 30.8% y/y. Wolfe and Jefferies checks confirm Rovo is in nearly every enterprise conversation with migrations accelerating.

bullets.title: NOW: Strongest enterprise software checks; large deals, PubSec strength, no quarter-end theatrics
bullets.body: Multiple channel checks from Wolfe, Jefferies, and Zukin's weekly all flag ServiceNow as the strongest enterprise software name heading into earnings — large deals, public sector/federal momentum, and no end-of-quarter pressure tactics. Wolfe describes infrastructure software as 'red hot' with AI adoption broadening.
